messages.content: Help me track the 'submitForm' action on a 'formHandler' object but only when the form has is required and is valid email validation flags set?

function.name: trackSubmitWithValidation
function.description: This function tracks the 'submitForm' action on a given object. It only logs the submission when specific validation flags are set; if the flags are not set, the original action is performed without tracking. Note that the provided function is in JavaScript syntax.

obj.description: The object with the 'submitForm' action to track. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

validationFlags.description: An array of validation flags required to trigger tracking. Possible options are isRequired, isValidEmail. This is JavaScript array type parameter in string representation. The list elements are of type String; they are not in string representation.

message.reasoning:
We need to call the function trackSubmitWithValidation with obj: "formHandler" and validationFlags: ["isRequired", "isValidEmail"]. The function expects obj as string representation of the object. So we pass "formHandler". validationFlags is a string representation of a JavaScript array type parameter. The list elements are of type String; they are not in string representation. So we need to pass something like '["isRequired","isValidEmail"]'? Wait: The description: "An array of validation flags required to trigger tracking. Possible options are isRequired, isValidEmail. This is JavaScript array type parameter in string representation. The list elements are of type String; they are not in string representation." That means we should pass a string that represents an array of strings. So we pass '["isRequired","isValidEmail"]'. But the elements are strings, not string representation. So we don't wrap them in quotes? Actually they are strings, so they need quotes. But the array itself is string representation. So we pass '["isRequired","isValidEmail"]'. That seems correct.
